newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt awards oil concession to Tunisian company.
newsitem.headline: Egypt awards oil concession to Tunisian company.

text.p: Egypt has awarded the South Dabaa oil exploration block to the private-sector Tunisian company HBS (Habib Bouchamaoui and Sons), an official of the state's Egyptian General Petroleum Corp (EGPC) said on Tuesday.
"HBS was the winner out of eight bids for South Dabaa," said Wafik Meshref, EGPC vice chairman for agreements.
South Dabaa is an onshore block of 1,500 square km in the western desert about half way between the city of Alexandria and the coastal town of Marsa Matrouh.
Meshref told Reuters the EGPC bid committee made the award this month but he could not give details of the conditions until it goes to a higher level for approval.

He said EGPC had looked at five bids for the Northeastern Desert block and asked three applicants to resubmit. "Two bids were close but needed more detailed study. The committee will meet by the end of December to decide," he added.
A Russian company had held the Northeastern Desert block but had to relinquish it because the Russian authorities would not release the money it needed to invest in Egypt.
Meshref said the bid committee also planned to award the Central Sinai and North Gharib blocks by the end of the year.
Central Sinai is an onshore block of 18,150 square km. North Gharib is an offshore block of 712 square km in the Gulf of Suez.
